deny-list mode leaves images unrestricted, and an exec no command rule refuses is the image floor's: the supervisor's own line (tier landlock, the fanotify listener) says allow unmatched, but where a decision plane records execs the kernel's terminal line is written by observe's matchExec, which names every exec no entry matches observed (rules.go), and compile --test's plane column says allow unmatched. Not a fail-open (the run allows the exec); the same split holds for any run whose images are unrestricted, with or without command rules, and is open in ADR 0048's implementation notes (2026-10-06). Only where the kernel makes BPF perf links (bpf_perf_link, a probe): the kernel's line is the terminal one only where the exec outcome links (tracepoint/syscalls/sys_exit_execve and sys_exit_execveat) attach, and they attach only as BPF perf links, upstream 5.15 and backported to RHEL 9.8's 5.14.0-687, where both cells disagree so on the stock AlmaLinux 9.8 guest (2026-11-10). On the RHEL 9 kernel of 2026-10-16 doctor reported them unavailable, the supervisor kept every exec's line, and both cells passed; a kernel bound could not tell those two 5.14 kernels apart
